messages:
terry: Heads-up — noticed a p95 bump for callback endpoints after the rollout this morning. p50 looks steady, p99 unchanged. Anyone else seeing this in the console?

marta: I saw the alert. p95 jumped ~120ms for /v1/callbacks POST in us-west-2 routes around 08:12.

jiwon: Can you paste the console query you used? I'm trying to reproduce.

terry: Query I used: `service:inference route:callbacks env:prod | percentile(latency_ms, 95) by endpoint, route`. On dashboard the series aligns with rollout window.

metrics-bot: Alert: p95 latency for /v1/callbacks exceeded threshold (200ms) at 2026-03-21 08:12:45 — sample count 340 (last 5m).

sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) routing policy change pushed some traffic to a fallback variant with higher tail; 2) quota throttling causing retries/higher latencies.

diego: We did push a routing weight tweak at 08:10 for canary -> main (0.02 -> 0.2). That could increase contention on one pool.

marta: Interesting — rollout notes said fallback model/variant still uses same instance-type but different cache warming. Could be KV cache cold start affecting mid-tail.

terry: If it's cache warming, I'd expect p99 to move too. p99 is flat which makes me think it's a sampling/aggregation artifact.

jiwon: Good point. Could be that dashboard's percentile derivation changed when we enabled sample-weighted rollups last week. Maybe p95 is now sampled differently than p99.

sam: We have two aggregations: 'streamed tdigest rollup' for pcts and 'exact' for p99 on recent data. If sampling weights were applied only to one path, you can get p95 shifts without p99 moving.

diego: Can you check the route tag propagation? If route tag was lost, queries by route might mix in higher-latency internal-only traffic.

marta: I checked: route tag present in 99% of events. The spike aligns with traffic that hit the canary variant weight bump.

terry: Quick reproducible check request: run the console query scoped to model_variant and include sample_count. `percentile(latency_ms,95) by model_variant, endpoint, sample_count` — compare counts between variants.

jiwon: Running now... results: canary variant p95=220ms sample_count=38, main variant p95=110ms sample_count=302. Combined p95=130ms.

sam: That pattern supports the 'small high-latency cohort' effect — small noisy canary pushes combined p95 up but p99 dominated by main variant tail.

diego: So it's not a telemetry bug, more of an explainable mix effect. Do we want to surface variant-level percentiles in the rollout UI?

marta: Yes — current rollout UI only shows endpoint-level p50/p95/p99. For rollouts we should show variant split and per-variant pX and sample counts.

jiwon: Agreed. Also add a note about sample counts and confidence intervals. Low-count variants should show CI or a warning badge.

sam: Ops ask: for quota routing, when a tenant hits reserved capacity and we fallback, show the fallback fraction and its latency separately. That'll help on-call triage.

terry: Action items: 1) Diego to add variant breakdown to the rollout dashboard (small change) 2) Jiwon to add sample-count/CI badge to percentile tiles 3) Marta to add a short blurb in the alert explaining "small cohort influence" and link to run the model_variant query.

diego: I'll open a PR for the rollout UI breakdown. ETA EOD.

jiwon: I'll prototype the CI badge; posting PoC in #eng-platform later today.

marta: I'll update the alert message and add a runbook snippet.

terry: Thanks — that'll reduce noisy pager churn. :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: Note: remember to document the aggregator differences (tdigest vs exact) in the telemetry README so future folks don't assume parity.

sam: Re: long-term: suggest adding a small built-in "influence" metric that shows the delta when excluding small variants — could auto-surface when variant sample < 5% of total.

marta: Love that idea. Filing a follow-up RFC after the UI/alert fixes.

terry: OK closing this thread for now, moving items to the eng-platform board. Ping if anything else shows up. :white_check_mark:
